dossier.public_summary: This 13.6-day dip does not repeat consistently. Odd transits are about ten times shallower than even ones and the measured depth jumps from essentially zero in one sector to more than 1% in another, with the signal dominated by two deep events. Together with a very low planet classifier rank, the pattern matches an eclipsing binary or systematic artefact seen at a different period, not a planetary transit.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even depth difference with odd much shallower than even, as expected for an eclipsing binary at twice the period (13.6 d here vs 27.2 d). Two sectors have >3 sigma odd-even, same sign, ruling out a planet with equal odd/even depths.
Individual transit depths are extremely inconsistent, carried by two deep events from one sector; typical planet transits are consistent. Supports noise/systematics or a blend rather than a planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent 1.1498202774983923e-13 share_of_top_3 0.979 outliers 15245 ppm (5.2 sigma), 8798 ppm (4.5 sigma), -266 ppm (-4.1 sigma)

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically between sectors even within the same pipeline (TESS-SPOC p_constant 3.907777954657993e-05), with sector 42 at -266 ppm and sector 92 at 11000 ppm. A real on-target planet should be steady within one source, not change sign.

Independent classifier ranks as strongly non-planet-like, despite a formally flat-bottomed shape and low impact parameter; flat bottom and short duration ratio 1.242 do not outweigh the significant odd-even and depth-change evidence, which also can occur in diluted eclipsing binaries.
